text: I think Haaland accidentally proved something that women have been trying to tell men for years. I think a lot of men think we just love Haaland because he's tall, rich, and famous, but there's tons of tall, rich, and famous dudes out there that women aren't obsessing over in the same way. And if you want women to pine over you the way we're pining over Haaland, let me give you some tips. I think most women are reacting to how he comes across. He seems so incredibly emotionally regulated. It also doesn't seem like he's constantly trying to prove himself, and he's playful, and he's a little weird, and he doesn't seem obsessed with, like, proving that he's cool. Women aren't just, like, looking for what you have. They're looking for how you move through the world. I found this video quite interesting, and I have nothing against Haaland. Great guy, great energy, funny memes. I also have nothing against this lady. I generally agree with the overall message she's sending. I often say in my own videos that you should work on yourself as a whole. Your appearance, career, social circle, personality, and yes, how you move through the world. But I do want to use this video as a logical exercise, since many of you keep asking me for examples of how to debate someone's argument. So, nothing personal here. This is just a logical exercise. The point of debate is right on the surface. She's basically saying that women are not pining for Haaland because he's tall, rich, famous, and, let me add, quite good-looking. They are reacting to how he comes across and moves through the world. So, in a very simplified form, the argument is that women are attracted to his energy rather than to his looks and social status. And to corroborate that, she then says that there are plenty of tall, rich, and famous men whom women do not obsess over in the same way. Fair enough. I think that is probably true. But this logic is still incomplete if you want to use it to show that Haaland's appeal comes mainly from his energy rather than his appearance, money, and status. To make that argument much stronger, she would need to provide examples of men who are not that tall, good-looking, rich, famous, or successful, but who have a similar kind of energy. And women still pine for them to a similar degree. That would support her point much better. Because then you could say, look, this man doesn't possess all of Haaland's obvious advantages, but women still react strongly to him because of how he carries himself. And if it is difficult to name examples like that, then, at the very least, Haaland's appeal is clearly not just about his energy. His height, appearance, success, wealth, and fame are probably doing quite a lot of heavy lifting as well. Then, if I were actually debating her, I would also need to provide a counterexample to make my own argument stronger. Someone who is tall, rich, successful, famous, and good-looking, but doesn't have Haaland's particular energy, and yet still has plenty of women pining for him. And I think there are many possible examples, with the most obvious one being Cristiano Ronaldo. I think most people would agree that Ronaldo's energy is very different from Haaland's. He appears far more image-conscious, competitive, and interested in projecting his status. He certainly doesn't come across as the slightly awkward, goofy Viking who is completely unconcerned with looking cool. And yet, somehow, I doubt Cristiano Ronaldo is suffering from a severe shortage of female attention. So, there you go. That is one simple way to examine an argument. First, identify what evidence would actually prove the person's point, and then look for a counterexample that could weaken it. And, by the way, my point is not that energy doesn't matter and that attraction is only about height, appearance, fame, and money. Energy absolutely matters. Personality matters. Confidence matters. How you make other people feel matters. My point is that all of these things matter together. That is precisely why it is important to develop yourself overall, rather than searching for one magical personality trait that supposedly overrides everything else. Anyway, I hope you found this video interesting, and hollup, hollup!
